description.narrative:
In early 2020, a group of young creatives living in the Dardesa informal settlement along the Kenya/Somalia border started sewing African dresses using a donated Juki sewing machine from a retired seamstress. The group soon realized that fashion and culture were powerful mediums through which diverse cultural and social experiences of migrant communities could be acknowledged and celebrated.
Thus, the birth of Mayhem Threads has continued to articulate young migrants’ journeys through storytelling workshops and continuesto explore ways in which fabric and stitch can be uniquely expressive and inclusive, recognizing the creative value of diversity through each person’s lived experiences.
Mayhem Threads is dedicated to protecting and empowering asylum seekers and refugees in camps with little support from existing humanitarian agencies, not only in Dardesa but also in Libat, Digira, and Ela—sleepy settlement schemes scattered along the Kenya/Somalia border. We operate at the intersection of fashion,sustainability, and social impact, offering asylum seekers an opportunity to rebuild their lives through meaningful work in garment production, tailoring, and design. By fostering economic independence, Mayhem Threads creates a pathway for social and professional integration for project participants with few resources and opportunities
With most humanitarian agencies based and focused on Dadaab, most of the asylum seekers and refugees in Dardesa and the other smaller settlement schemes acutely lack resources and struggle to access basic commodities like water, pit latrines, food, and basic health.
Our project seeks to strengthen marginalized communities' voices through: 1. Skills Training <(>&<)> Workforce Development—Mayhem Threads provides hands-on vocational training in tailoring, embroidery, and textile design, equipping refugees with employable skills. With 12 pioneer founders having experience in the garment industry, new members are in good hands for their sewing journey 2. Community Empowerment<(>&<)> Support—By fostering a supportive network, Mayhem Threads helps asylum seekers gain confidence and build new relationships. Our connection with like-minded organizations like R NetworQ has strengthenedour ability to provide capacity-building and networking opportunities for asylum seekers, refugees, and migrants 3. Market Access <(>&<)> Brand Development—We effectively market handmade, refugee-crafted clothing and accessories, promoting diversity and social entrepreneurship. 4. Advocacy <(>&<)> Awareness—MayhemThreads actively raises awareness about refugee rights, ethical labor practices,and the intersection of fashion and social justice. 5. Elevating Refugee Voices—We employ human rights-centered capacity-building initiatives to work with local grassroots organizations, including queer, refugee-led groups. Through mentorship, peer learning sessions, networking opportunities, and the development of storytelling tools, MayHem helps local organizations enhance their service to the community and thus expand refugee voices

participating-org.narrative:
We assist asylum seekers, migrants, and refugees at the Kenya/Somalia border at every step of their journey, working along displacement routes and in transit towns. We provide them with much-needed emergency support, and temporary safe shelter and connect them with the resources and opportunities they need to build safe, stable, and empowered lives
Vision: A world where asylum seekers and refugees at the Kenya/Somalia border are empowered to build safe, stable, and fulfilling lives, free from displacement and hardship.
Mission: To walk alongside displaced individuals at every stage of their journey, providing immediate emergency aid, safe shelter, and critical resources while fostering long-term resilience and self-reliance. We operate along displacement routes and in transit towns to ensure protection, opportunity, and advocacy for those rebuilding their lives.
Objectives - Provide immediate emergency aid to asylum seekers and refugees arriving at the border. - Offer safe and temporary shelter for those in transit. - Empower refugees and asylum seekers to become self-sufficient and integrated into their new communities. - Connect refugees to resource access - education, legal assistance, livelihood training, and psychosocial support for sustainable stability. - Amplify displaced voices and collaborate with stakeholders to uphold human rights and equitable policies. - Strengthen resilience through skill-building, peer networks, and participatory programs that restore agency.
